description: We are a passionate team interested in space exploration, technology, and innovation. Through COSMIC LENS, we aim to make NASA SPHEREx data easier to explore by visualizing infrared images, comparing observations over time, and identifying possible cosmic changes. We are looking for enthusiastic teammates with skills in AI/ML, Python, web development, astronomy, data visualization, and UI/UX design who are excited to learn, collaborate, and build something meaningful together.
summary:
COSMIC LENS – SPHEREx Universe is an interactive web-based astronomical exploration platform designed to make space science more accessible, engaging, and understandable. The platform allows users to explore astronomical observations, discover space images, and compare changes in the universe through interactive visualization.

The application integrates SPHEREx-related astronomical data and NASA image resources to provide users with an engaging space exploration experience. It includes three major features: Cosmic Time Machine, which allows users to compare astronomical images from different observation periods using an interactive Before-and-After slider; Galaxy Explorer, which provides an organized visual exploration of astronomical images; and Sky Explorer, which enables users to search astronomical archives using observation IDs and sky coordinates.

Additionally, the homepage includes a Global Icon that navigates users to a dedicated IRSA (Infrared Science Archive) page. This page provides access to astronomical archive resources and includes an integrated AI Assistant. Users can ask questions about SPHEREx, astronomical observations, infrared data, and space exploration to receive informative explanations.

The main objective of COSMIC LENS is to transform complex astronomical data into an interactive visual learning experience and encourage users to explore and understand the universe through technology.
details:
COSMIC LENS – SPHEREx Universe is an interactive web-based platform designed to make astronomical data exploration simple, visual, and engaging. It helps users explore the universe through astronomical images, infrared observations, and space archive data.

The platform provides three major features:

  1. Cosmic Time Machine: Allows users to compare astronomical images from different observation periods using an interactive Before-and-After slider. Users can move the slider to visually explore changes between two observations of the same region.
  2. Galaxy Explorer: Provides an organized image exploration interface where users can browse astronomical images, view image previews, and explore available observation details.
  3. Sky Explorer: Allows users to search astronomical archives using observation IDs and celestial coordinates such as Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (DEC). Users can explore matching observations, image previews, and available astronomical metadata.

Additionally, the homepage includes a Global Icon that navigates users to a dedicated IRSA (Infrared Science Archive) page. This page provides access to infrared astronomical resources and an AI Assistant where users can ask questions about SPHEREx, infrared observations, astronomical discoveries, and space exploration.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

The project makes complex astronomical information easier to understand through interactive visual experiences. It encourages students, researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts to explore astronomical data, compare observations, and learn about the universe. It also improves accessibility to scientific information through a user-friendly interface.

Technologies Used:

  • Frontend: React.js, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Tailwind CSS
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • Astronomical Data: SPHEREx data resources, NASA Images API, and IRSA archive services
  • Visualization: Interactive image viewers and timeline comparison
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code and GitHub
  • Deployment: Vercel and Render

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative aspect of COSMIC LENS is its combination of astronomical archive exploration and interactive visual storytelling. Instead of presenting scientific data only as text or technical records, the platform allows users to visually compare astronomical observations, explore different sky positions, and discover information through an AI-assisted experience.

Factors Considered:

The team considered data accuracy, image availability, user experience, accessibility, responsive design, reliable API integration, and the ability to present complex astronomical information in a simple and engaging way.

Our ultimate goal is to make exploring the universe an interactive learning experience and bring astronomical discoveries closer to everyone.
